population: ischaemic cardiomyopathy, EF <=40% by MRI, infarct >=5% LV
finding: 60 patients randomised 1:1:1 to four placebo, one UC-MSC + three placebo, or four UC-MSC doses of 100M cells IV. Primary endpoint change in LVEF by cardiac MRI at 12 months. 47 enrolled as of 2025-11-30; follow-up to March 2027. No efficacy result yet.
citation: Bolli R et al. Design and rationale of CATO, a Phase IIA randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of single or repeated intravenous UC-MSCs in ischemic cardiomyopathy. Am Heart J 294 (April 2026).

population: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (NOT ischaemic heart disease)
finding: Four IV infusions of 150M CDCs every 3 months, randomised double-blind placebo-controlled. First repeat sequential cell dosing for a cardiac indication. Upper-limb function benefit. Repeat dosing recruits adaptive immunity, untested before this trial.
citation: McDonald CM et al. Repeated intravenous cardiosphere-derived cell therapy in late-stage Duchenne muscular dystrophy (HOPE-2). Lancet 2022;399:1049-58.

finding: 60 patients randomised to two transendocardial CD34+ doses 6 months apart or one. **No difference versus single dose** on LVEF, volumes, exercise tolerance or NT-proBNP at 1 year. Only 10 of 30 responded to the second dose (>=5 pp LVEF); responders had lower pre-dose LVEF than non-responders (34.9% vs 40.0%, p=0.02), indicating a ceiling effect.
citation: Vrtovec B et al. Effects of Repetitive Transendocardial CD34+ Cell Transplantation in Patients With Nonischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy. Circ Res 2018;123:389-396.

finding: Three arms: single dose, two doses 3 months apart, placebo. Two doses beat one dose beat control on LVEF, LV volumes and scar size.
citation: Yao et al. Two intracoronary BM-MNC doses 3 months apart after first STEMI with LVEF 20-39%; n=39, MRI/SPECT endpoints.

finding: Two doses 6 months apart produced a more pronounced LVEF improvement than a single dose. Not placebo-controlled.
citation: Gu et al. Repeated intracoronary mononuclear cell infusion at 6 months in ischaemic heart failure; n=45.

finding: Three doses of 12M CPCs 35 days apart versus ONE dose of the same total 36M cells. Cumulative LVEF gain +13.0 +/-0.8 pp versus +4.7 +/-0.8 pp (p<0.01), roughly triple. Increments per dose +3.4, +4.0, +5.5 pp. Formation of new cardiomyocytes was negligible in all groups: the effect cannot be ascribed to differentiation. The two extra injections could not be replaced by tripling the single dose.
citation: Guo Y, ... Bolli R. Repeated Administrations of Cardiac Progenitor Cells Are Markedly More Effective Than a Single Administration: A New Paradigm in Cell Therapy. Circ Res 2016;119:545-557.

finding: Three 12M doses beat one 36M dose: LVEF +13.1 +/-1.3 pp versus +0.8 +/-3.1 pp. Repeated doses reduced collagen and immune infiltration; the single dose did not. New cardiomyocyte formation negligible.
citation: Repeated Administrations of Cardiac Progenitor Cells Are Superior to a Single Administration of an Equivalent Cumulative Dose. J Am Heart Assoc 2018;7:e007400.

population: pig, chronic ischaemic cardiomyopathy, reperfused MI
finding: Three IV MSC doses 35 days apart beat one dose on three independent modalities (echo, MRI, haemodynamics); reduced fibrosis and hypertrophy. Very few IV cells reach the heart and they do not engraft, so 'myocardial regeneration is not plausible'; mechanism is systemic anti-inflammatory. Direct preclinical basis for CATO.
citation: Tang XL et al. Intravenous infusions of mesenchymal stromal cells have cumulative beneficial effects in a porcine model of chronic ischaemic cardiomyopathy. Cardiovasc Res 2024;120:1939-1953.

finding: Explicitly proposes replacing the fixed inter-dose interval with response-guided timing: monitor serially and re-dose when the effect of the previous dose ceases, rather than at an arbitrary fixed interval. Proposed, NOT tested. This is the open loop ATLAS-3 assumed.
citation: Bolli R, Hare JM. Potential Strategies for Clinical Translation of Repeated Cell Therapy. Circ Res 2019;124:1088-1090.

population: mouse MI, human cardiac progenitor cells, n=34-37
finding: Day-1 PET reporter-gene signal predicts later function: rho=0.76 with week-2 echocardiographic function and rho=0.80 with cardiac MRI LVEF (p<0.0001). Low-engraftment animals showed no significant functional gain. This is a measured, published feedback signal quality - but in mice, with a reporter gene the cells must be engineered to carry.
citation: Early Stem Cell Engraftment Predicts Late Cardiac Functional Recovery: Preclinical Insights From Molecular Imaging. Circ Cardiovasc Imaging 2012;5:391-401.

population: rat heart, human endothelial progenitor cells
finding: Iron-oxide MRI signal was unchanged for 7 days while reporter-gene PET became undetectable by day 7 and histology showed extensive apoptosis. Iron is phagocytosed by macrophages after the cells die, so iron MRI localises but does NOT measure viability. Only reporter-gene PET tracked living cells.
citation: Combined Reporter Gene PET and Iron Oxide MRI for Monitoring Survival and Localization of Transplanted Cells in the Rat Heart. J Nucl Med 2009;50:1088-1094.

finding: Acute retention was statistically similar by intramyocardial (13.4 +/-3.4 %ID) and intracoronary (17.4 +/-4.1 %ID) delivery, yet engrafted cells were detected histologically only after intramyocardial injection. Acute retention does NOT correlate with engraftment.
citation: Non-invasive in vivo imaging of cardiac stem/progenitor cell biodistribution and retention after intracoronary and intramyocardial delivery in a swine model. J Transl Med 2017;15:57.
